title: Route normalization + templating for metrics (shared utility + dual-emit migration)
author: Thomas Baird
description: Summary: Introduces a shared route normalization/templating library used by the API gateway and telemetry emitters to reduce metrics/tag cardinality while preserving debuggability. We now emit both the raw route and a canonicalized route template during the migration window (backward compatible for existing dashboards/queries). Motivation: Our current `http.route` / `api_route` tags are a mix of literal paths (high cardinality) and partially templated variants (inconsistent grouping). This makes route-level cost attribution noisy and can cause warehouse partition skew. This PR standardizes normalization rules (UUID/numeric/ULID segments, base64-ish blobs, common resource IDs) and provides a single implementation shared across services. Key changes: (1) New package `pkg/routing/normalize` with deterministic templating rules and an allowlist for known Redwood + OpenAI-compat endpoints; (2) Gateway and request-middleware now populate `route_template` (e.g. `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/files/{file_id}`) plus `route_raw` (original path) and `route_source` (router | fallback); (3) Telemetry emitters updated to tag events with `route_template` as the primary dimension while continuing to emit the previous tag (`api_route`) as an alias to avoid breaking existing dashboards; (4) Guardrails: max segments, max template tokens, and fallback to `/unknown` when parsing fails; (5) Extensive tests for edge cases (streaming, OpenAI compat, trailing slashes, query strings, internal admin routes). Migration plan: Phase 1 (this PR): dual-emit (`route_template` + legacy `api_route`), keep consumers unchanged. Phase 2 (follow-up): warehouse jobs and dashboards switch to `route_template`. Phase 3 (90 days after Phase 2): deprecate legacy tag emission once all known consumers are migrated. Notes: This is intended to unblock route+model cost breakdowns in Console usage insights by ensuring stable route grouping across regions and deployments.

gateway: populate route_template/route_raw tags (dual emit) for requests
metrics: migrate metering + tracing emitters to prefer route_template
tests: add fixtures for openai-compat + streaming edge cases
docs: add migration notes + examples for dashboard authors

services/telemetry-ingest: event tag mapping for route dims (dual emit)
pkg/metrics: tag keys + helper to avoid accidental raw-route emission
tests: unit tests + golden fixtures for templating
illustrative_snippet: Before (inconsistent): api_route="/v1/files/3f2c1a3b-7a2c-4b0d-b9b8-7c9f4c1a7c1d/content"; After (stable): route_template="/v1/files/{file_id}/content" route_raw="/v1/files/3f2c1a3b-7a2c-4b0d-b9b8-7c9f4c1a7c1d/content" route_source="router" legacy api_route continues to emit as an alias to route_template during migration.
review_conversation: Logan Wright: Can you clarify the precedence rules when both router-based templates and fallback templating are available? We should always prefer the router’s route name if present. Thomas Baird (author): Yep — updated `route_source` to `router` when mux exposes a named route; fallback only runs when the router cannot produce a template (e.g., older internal handlers). Added a test for the router-precedence behavior. Nadia Rahman: For cost attribution we need retries/fallback requests to still show the original API route when possible. Are we losing that by templating? Thomas Baird: We keep `route_raw` for debugging and also continue emitting the legacy `api_route` tag as an alias so existing attribution queries don’t break. The aggregation pipeline will use `route_template` as the group-by dimension but can still drill into raw samples when investigating anomalies. Chloe Martin: Naming: please avoid calling this just “route” since some services also tag “endpoint”. Can we standardize on `route_template` and `route_raw`? Thomas Baird: Done — renamed from `normalized_route` to `route_template` across gateway + telemetry to match docs/UX language. Allison Grant: Cardinality guardrail: what happens when a path has 12 segments or includes random blobs that don’t match patterns? We can’t accidentally emit raw strings as tags. Thomas Baird: Implemented hard caps (`maxSegments=8`, `maxTemplateTokens=4`) and a strict “no-raw-on-failure” rule that maps to `/unknown`. Added metrics counter `route_template_fallback_total{reason=...}` so we can alert if this spikes. Kaitlyn Nguyen: Any security concerns with `route_raw` being logged/exported? Ensure we don’t include query params and that we strip fragments. Thomas Baird: Confirmed query params are stripped (`/path?x=1` -> `/path`). Added a test that ensures `route_raw` never includes `?` and explicitly excludes headers/body. Also `route_raw` remains internal to telemetry events (not user-visible) and is behind existing log access controls.
requested_changes: Prefer router-provided template when available; add tests
Rename `normalized_route` -> `route_template` for consistency with Console terminology
Add hard guardrails to prevent accidental raw-route cardinality explosion
Strip query params from route_raw; add security-focused test
release_notes: Internal: Standardized route templating for telemetry tags to enable stable route-level usage/cost aggregation. Dual-emits legacy `api_route` during migration window.
